title: HuBMAP Tissue Sectioning for FFPE Specimens
author: Leigh Propper
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bahdib26

steps.title: Prepare tray and tissue blocks
steps.instruction: Place a few paper towels or Wypall on the microtome tray, dampen them with water, verify that each tissue block is correctly embedded, scrape all wax from the block sides, and label each block with case number, tissue type, and any other required identification.

steps.title: Fill and heat flotation bath
steps.instruction: Locate the tissue flotation (water) bath, fill it completely with de‑ionized or purified water, turn the bath on and set the water temperature to 42 °C.

steps.title: Inspect microtome
steps.instruction: Inspect the microtome to be used, confirming it is clean, well‑maintained, and set at the correct angle for sectioning.

steps.title: Label slides and gather supplies
steps.instruction: Using a pencil or specialized slide marker, label each microscope slide with the appropriate case number, tissue type, and test; locate the correct glass‑charged slides for the tissue, and wear gloves to keep slides free of debris and ink.

steps.title: Install microtome blade
steps.instruction: Select a fresh blade from its storage container, place it in the microtome’s knife holder, secure it with the knife clamp/lock spanner, and engage the locking lever under the flywheel.

steps.title: Mount tissue block in microtome
steps.instruction: After double‑checking all microtome settings, retrieve a tissue block from the ice tray and secure it in the microtome chuck (block holder).

steps.title: Roughly advance blade to block
steps.instruction: Using the coarse advance wheel on the left side, carefully bring the blade close to the block and cut a few thin sections to confirm proper positioning; adjust as needed.

steps.title: Trim block to expose tissue
steps.instruction: Trim gently into the block to expose a representative tissue surface, cutting at a thickness of 10–30 µm; this can be done with the advance flywheel alone or with a combination of advance and coarse wheels using the rocking method.

steps.title: Chill trimmed block on ice
steps.instruction: Return the trimmed block to the ice tray and let it chill for approximately 10–15 minutes; the cold wax provides support for harder tissue elements and the slight moisture from the ice aids cutting.

steps.title: Re‑mount chilled block for sectioning
steps.instruction: Remove the now‑cold block from the ice tray and secure it again in the microtome chuck, ready for precision sectioning.

steps.title: Position block near blade
steps.instruction: Using the coarse adjustment wheel on the left, move the block holder as close as possible to the knife edge without touching; stop when condensation droplets appear near the knife holder.

steps.title: Set thickness and start ribbon
steps.instruction: Unlock and rotate the hand wheel on the right to move the block holder up and down steadily; verify the micron thickness setting (normal 4–5 µm) before proceeding, and be prepared to discard the first few sections that may have artifacts.

steps.title: Transfer ribbon to water bath
steps.instruction: When a ribbon of wax and tissue forms on the front of the knife holder plate, use one pair of forceps to grip the bottom of the ribbon and another pair to grip the top near the blade, then gently pull the ribbon away from the microtome toward the water bath.

steps.title: Float ribbon and lay on water
steps.instruction: Shift the ribbon toward the water bath and, in a gentle dragging motion, lay it onto the surface of the 42 °C water; allow the sections to sit for a few moments so the heated water expands any compression and removes wrinkles.

steps.title: Select section from floating ribbon
steps.instruction: After the ribbon has floated for approximately 20–45 seconds, use forceps to pick the desired section from the water surface.

steps.title: Place section onto slide
steps.instruction: Locate the pre‑labeled microscope slide that matches the tissue block, dip the slide into the water bath, and position it adjacent to and slightly under the selected section.

steps.title: Adjust and lift section
steps.instruction: With forceps, adjust the section on the slide as needed, then lift the slide (with the section) out of the water bath.

steps.title: Dry slides
steps.instruction: Place the slide into a slide‑drying tray or staining rack; let the slides air‑dry overnight or dry them in a 50 °C oven for 1 hour.

steps.title: Remove and dispose of blade
steps.instruction: After the last block is sectioned, unlock the blade holder lever/spanner, use a magnet or forceps to remove the blade, and discard it in the waste container on the blade box or a sharps container; clean the microtome if work is finished for the day.

steps.title: Clean microtome and accessories
steps.instruction: Using a microtome brush (optionally with a light application of ParaGuard), brush away all tissue and paraffin remnants from the microtome, catch tray, chuck, and behind the knife holder; wipe the brush with gauze after use.

steps.title: Remove water bath dish
steps.instruction: Carefully lift the glass dish from the water bath and pour the remaining water into the nearest sink.

steps.title: Clean water bath
steps.instruction: Clean the emptied water bath with warm water and Dawn dish soap, rinse, and replace the dish on the water‑bath bench unit.
